reason: The framework core already exists in Go as package cordis in src/go, tracking upstream 86f59e4, which is 51 commits ahead of the harness's vendored rc.12. Seven of the 54 API rows the harness uses are gaps; six deliverables close them, and the JavaScript-only parts (proxy context, mixins, accessors, decorators) are replaced by typed keys.

Sixteen of the 22 helper names imported anywhere map to Go built-ins or the standard library (maps, slices, reflect.DeepEqual, encoding/base64, encoding/hex, time); the other six are the volatile config reference, which is not built: a live setting reaches a component through its update hook (DH-ADR-COSMOKIT-2, DH-ADR-LOADER-7).

The FIXME says the status event should carry richer fiber information than the previous state alone. The Go port's status notification is a typed callback that receives the fiber, the old state and the new state (Internal.OnStatus, src/go/cordis/tree.go:133), and DH-D-CORDIS-6 gives it a form owned by the subscribing fiber.

The TODO exists because JavaScript distinguishes synchronous validators from promise-returning ones and cordis rejects the latter. A Go schema is an ordinary function that may block, and the port calls it outside the tree lock (src/go/cordis/fiber.go:762-773), so there is no async case to add.

The TODO is a poor error from the mixin forwarder when the source service is missing. The Go design has no mixins or proxy context; a failed lookup returns a ServiceError that names the service and says whether it was undeclared or unavailable.

The override forces every request for the package to the vendored folder so the npm install tree holds one copy. Duplicate package copies are a property of npm and pnpm resolution; a Go build has exactly one copy of a package, and these helpers come from the Go standard library.

title: Lifecycle hardening exists only as local patch V6 on the vendored cordis and is not in upstream

reason: The guarantees of patch V6 (no effects while unloading, joined cleanup, pending effects drained, a child fiber owned before it is announced) become behaviour of the Go port with their own tests instead of a patch to re-apply at each sync.

title: Raw, effective and candidate config access exists only as local patch V15 across core, loader, include and HMR

reason: The Go port gains EffectiveConfig, ResolveConfig, RetainConfig and a fiber-owned config hook as first-class API, with the publication rules of the upstream spec files as tests.

title: Fifteen hand-written per-listener containment loops built on EventsService.dispatch(), which upstream cordis marks deprecated

reason: A Notify dispatch verb calls every listener and contains and logs each failure, so no caller enumerates callbacks by hand and no deprecated API is relied on.

title: Plugins detect their own disposal by listening to the tree-wide internal/plugin event and firing an AbortController

reason: Every loaded fiber exposes a standard cancellation context that is cancelled the moment the fiber is asked to unload, before the unload waits for the running body.

title: Proxy-based caller attribution has to be undone by hand with getTraceable and symbols.original

reason: The Go context is not a proxy and never swaps a service's context for the caller's; a method that registers on behalf of a caller takes the owner context explicitly or the service implements Scoped.

title: The vendored framework carries 21 logged local modifications that must be re-applied by hand at every upstream sync

reason: The Go port is first-party code with one recorded upstream revision and a sync table; harness requirements are implemented in it directly, so there is no patch log to re-apply.

title: The vendored cosmokit is no longer upstream cosmokit: V22 adds volatile references and changes what deepEqual means

reason: The debt is a vendored helper package that drifted from its upstream by gaining a reference type and a changed equality. The Go design has neither: there is no helper package and no reference type (a live setting reaches a component through its update hook), and config equality is plain structural equality with no special case.

title: cordis framework core: the existing Go port in src/go/cordis, extended
cosmokit utilities: the Go standard library; the volatile reference type is not built
The port follows upstream 86f59e4 and adds the harness's guarantees as its own features
No proxy context: typed keys and an explicit owner
Leaving is signalled by a cancellation context, not by an event
Two verbs for two contracts: Notify contains failures, Emit stops on the first
Scoped routing is a dispatcher feature; scope policy stays in the harness
No utility package; config equality stays plain
The volatile reference type is not built; a live setting reaches a component through its update hook
Unload is complete, exclusive and final
A cancellation context for every loaded fiber
Context values and scoped dispatch
Contained notification dispatch (Notify)
Raw, effective and candidate config, with a config hook
Lifecycle subscriptions owned by a fiber
An around key with separate request and result types
Strict config decoding: an unknown key is a config error
A tree is created with the log exporters its creator chooses
A cleanup observer on a tree
Read-only accessors for a fiber's children and provided services
Registrations are refused while a fiber unloads
Concurrent disposers join one cleanup and the provider outlives it
A pending fiber's effects are released and a creation handler can dispose the new fiber
The lifetime context is cancelled before unload waits for the body
Context values are inherited downwards only
A filtered dispatch reaches exactly the admitted and global listeners in every mode
Notify runs every listener despite errors and panics
Effective config is published only by a load or a current accepted update
A config hook can transform or reject its fiber's candidate and ends with its owner
Owned lifecycle subscriptions end with the subscriber
Existing port tests stay green and the rc.12 expectations are mapped to named Go tests
An around dispatch runs listeners outermost first, short-circuits, returns errors and panics as errors, and honours the filter
In a strict tree an unknown config key or trailing data fails the load; a lenient component and a non-strict tree are unaffected
A tree created with chosen exporters writes nothing to the standard streams and delivers every message to its exporters
The cleanup observer sees a start and an end per effect with fiber and label, and cannot disturb the unload
Children and Provides return current copies and are safe while the tree changes
Config equality is plain structural equality with no special case
